candidate_relations.reason: Lymphocytic colitis is a microscopic colitis without noncaseating granulomas throughout the gut.
Gastroesophageal reflux disease is a comorbid history, not sarcoidosis.
Whipple disease was specifically tested and negative.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Whipple disease vs sarcoid; Tropheryma negative

candidate_relations.reason: Primary biliary cholangitis is an autoimmune cholangiopathy not established here.
Gastrointestinal lymphoma is a neoplastic infiltrative disease, not noncaseating microgranulomas.
Common variable immunodeficiency can cause granulomas but is not described (no hypogammaglobulinemia).
Crohn disease is the principal granulomatous enterocolitis alternative and conflicts with a sarcoidosis diagnosis.
Hereditary hemochromatosis–associated GI disease attributes the granulomas to iron overload, which liver biopsy did not support as granulomatous.
Gastrointestinal amyloidosis is a deposition disease, not granulomatous.
Hemochromatosis is a documented comorbidity, not the granulomatous diagnosis.
Whipple's disease is the same excluded Tropheryma infection.
Granulomatosis with polyangiitis is a necrotizing ANCA vasculitis, not GI microgranulomas with a normal chest CT.
Graft-versus-host disease requires transplantation, which is absent.
Colitis is a parent symptom/pathology missing sarcoidosis.
Blau syndrome is a pediatric NOD2 granulomatous disease, not this adult presentation.
Hereditary hemochromatosis restates the iron-overload comorbidity.
Ulcerative colitis is a nongranulomatous IBD and does not fit pan-GI microgranulomas including ileum and stomach.
Celiac disease serologies were negative.
Autoimmune enteropathy is a different immune enteropathy without this granuloma pattern.
Idiopathic granulomatous gastritis captures gastric granulomas but not the pan-GI sarcoidosis diagnosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: idiopathic granulomatous gastritis missing systemic sarcoidosis

case_quality_flags: Noncaseating GI microgranulomas with raised ACE but unremarkable chest CT and liver biopsy without granulomas make isolated GI sarcoidosis a diagnosis of exclusion
